newsitem.title: UK: SFA fines Rothschild copper trader.
newsitem.headline: SFA fines Rothschild copper trader.

text.p: The Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) said on Tuesday it had fined Robert Lewis, a junior copper trader at N.M. Rothschild and Sons, for false entries in trading books.
The case arose between January 1 and March 6 1996, when Lewis was employed by Rothschild and had responsibility for recording copper trades with a duration of three months or less.
"Mr Lewis made false entries in three copper trading books which had the affect of moving profit from two other copper trading books to the book for which he had responsibility," the SFA said.
Although the false entries affected recorded profits on the three books, they did not affect the trading desk's overall profit and loss.
There was also no effect on external customers or counterparties. Lewis was fined 2,000 stg and severely reprimanded by the SFA.
